On the 600 map, Shaskanka is the kingdom of Gauda in Bengal under King Shashanka, who ruled from his capital Karnasuvarna from about 590 to the 620s. He is often called the first king of a united Bengal.

Shashanka rose as the Gupta world broke up. He fought for control of the Ganges plain and is said to have killed Rajyavardhana, the elder brother of Harsha. Harsha made war on him in alliance with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa, but Shashanka seems to have held Bengal until his death.

Buddhist writers, including Harsha's friend Xuanzang, accuse him of persecuting Buddhists and harming the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya. Historians treat this with caution. After his death Bengal fell into a long period of disorder, until the Pala Empire rose around 750.
